title: Selective vs. Differential Media

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: Selective media inhibit the growth of some organisms while allowing others to grow. Differential media allow multiple organisms to grow but let you visually distinguish between them based on a biochemical reaction.
explanation: A medium can be selective, differential, both, or neither. MacConkey agar, for example, is both selective (bile salts and crystal violet inhibit most Gram-positive organisms) and differential (lactose fermentation is indicated by a color change). Selectivity and differentiation are independent properties of a medium's formulation, not a single spectrum.

comparison.left: Selective: an inhibitory ingredient suppresses unwanted growth
comparison.right: Differential: an indicator ingredient reveals a metabolic difference

comparison.left: Bile salts, antibiotics, high salt/dye concentration
comparison.right: A fermentable sugar plus a pH or redox indicator

commonMisconceptions: That a medium must be one or the other — many common media are both at once.
